Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
STYRENATED PHENOL 

( First Revision } 



0. FOREWORD 

0*1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Inciian 
Standards Institution on 27 March 1985, after the draft finalized by the 
Rubber Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 

©•2 This standard was originally published in 1974. In this revision, 
the requirements of refractive index and relative density have been 
modified. 

0.3 Styrenated phenols are non-staining and non-disclouring antioxidants 
finding application in white and transparent vulcanizates. In this 
standard the requirements pcrtaininjT to the pioduct obtained by aryja- 
ting phenol with styrcne only is consideied. This is essentially a mixture 
of mono-, di-and tri-styrenated phenol with molecular mass rani<ing 
from 200 to 400. This product is soluble in benzene, acetone, ethyl 
alcohol and petroleum ether and insoluble in water. 

0.4 Besides specifying chemical requirements, tlie standard includoN a 
recommended procedure for evaluating ihe material by means of a 
standard compounding and vulcanizing procedure. 

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whetlier a particular n^quircnient of this 
stantlard is complied with, the final value, ob>erve(l or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded ofT in accord- 
ance with IS : 2-h)60*, The number of sii^n'Ticant places retained in 
the rounded off value should bo the vame as tliat of the specified value 
in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This stanrlard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampl'ng 
and test for styrenated phenol intended for use as an antioxidant in 
rubber compoimds. 

♦Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). 

3 



IS s 7351 - 1985 

2. REQjlTIllEMENTS 

2.1 Description — The material shall be in the form of a clear viscous 
liquid not darker than pale amber colour. It shall not contain any 
visible impurities. 

2.2 The material shall comply with the requirements given in Table 1 
when tested according to the methods given in Appendix A. Reference 
to the relevant clauses of Appendix A is given in col 4 of Table 1.

2«2«1 All the tests shall be carried out within one month of receipt 
of the material by the purchaser. 

2*3 Compoundiiig — The material when compounded and tested as 
given in Appendix B shall have its performance comparable with that of 
a sample, previously approved by the purchaser complying with the 
requirements given in 2.1 and 2.2. 

3. PACKING AND MARKING 

3.1 Packing — The material shall be packed in 25 kg and 200 kg drums 
or as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 

3.2 Marking — The packages shall be securely sealed and legibly 
marked with the following information: 

a) Manufacturer's name and registered trade-mark, if any; 

b) Chemical name or trade name of the material; 

c) Net mass of the package; and 

d) The lot and the batch number. 



IS I 7351 - 1965 

3.2.1 The packagei may also be marked with the I SI Certification 
Mark. 

NoTB — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the proviiiont of the 
Indian Standard! Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regu- 
lations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the require* 
ments of that standard under a well-defined s\ .stem of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI 
marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, 
may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. 

4. SAMPUNG AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 
4.1 Sampling 

4.1.1 Lot — All the containers in a single consignment manufactured 
under the same condition shall constitute a lot. 

4.1.2 Samples shall be tested for each lot separately for ascertaining 
the conformity of the material to the requirements of the specification. 

4.1.5 The number of containers to be chosen from the lot shall be in 
accordance with Table 2.

APPENDIX A 

( Table 1 ) 
TEST METHODS FOR STYRENATED PHENOL 

A-l. QUALITY OF REAGENTS 

A-1.1 Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water 
( se0 IS : 1070-1977* ) shall be employed in the tests. 

NoTS — 'Pure chemicab' shall mean chemicaii that do not contain impurities 
which affect the results of test or analysis. 

*Specification for water for general laboratory use ( sieoni rtoitim ). 

5 



IS s 7351 - 1985 

A-2. DETERMINATION OF REFRACTIVE INDEX 

A«2*l Apparatus 

A-2*l*l Abbe-refractometer of standard make covering a range of 
1 '300 to 1 '700 suitable for reading up to fourth place of decimal and 
provided with thermostat. 

A-2.2 Procedure 

A-2.2.1 Start the thermostat attached to the apparatus and wait till it 
attains a constant temperature at 27'0 ± 0'5°C, Clean the prism with 
cotton soaked with alcohol and wait till alcohol is evaporated off. 

A-2.2.2 Transfer a drop of styrenated phenol on the prism with the 
help of a clean, dry glass rod and close the prism carefully. Adjust the 
eye piece in such a manner that the cross wires coincide with the line of 
demarcation between bright and dark region. Read the result on the 
dial to fourth place of decimal with the help of the vernier scale. 

A-2.3 Precautions 

a) Check occasionally the readings of the instrument with test 
sample; 

b) Temperature should be controlled within the limit of ± 1*C; 

c) Clean the prism with alcohol; 

d) Put right quantity of liquid on the prism; and 

e) There should be no air bubble in the sample while taking 
reading. 

A^. DETERMINATION OF RELATIVE DENSITY 

A-3.1 Apparatus 

A-3J.1 Hydrontiter — with a range of 1000 to 11 10. 

A-3.1.2 Measuring Cylinder — 100-mL Internal diameter 28 mm and 
internal height 250 mm. 

A-3.1.3 Thermostat 

A-3.2 Proeadare -- Fill styrenated phenol in a clean, dry, measuring 
cylinder to 100 ml mark ( approximately ) and place the cylinder in a 
thermostat. Start the thermostat and wait till it attains a constant 
temperature at 27 db I'^C. Check that the material has also attained the 
set temperature. Now allow the clean, dry, hydrometer to be immersed 
in the liquid and wait till it assumes a steady position. The reading 
corresponding to the meniscus of the liquid will give the relative density 
of the sample. 



IS : 7351 - 1985 

A*S«3 Precautions 

a) Avoid any entrapment of air bubbles in the f amples; 

b) Take care that the hydrometer does not touch the cylinder wall, 
and 

c) While taking readings position of eye should be on the same level 
as of the meniscus. 

A-4. DETERMINATION OF VISCOSITY 

A-4.0 General — The measurement of the drag produced upon a given 
spindle rotating at a definite constant speed while immersed in the 
material at a given temperature and indicated on a dial produces 
viscosity readings in centipoise. 

A-4.1 Apparatus 

A-4.1.1 Brook Field Synchro Electric Viscometer. 

A-4.2 Procedure 

A-4.2.1 Support the viscometer on the stand and level. Attach 
spindle No. '^ by holding the upper shaft coupling and turning the 
spindle. Place sample in as wide a container as possible that will give 
the proper depth and adjust to 27 ± 1*C. Lower the instrument so 
that the spindle is immersed in the liquid to the groove on the spindle. 
Check levelling and centre spindle by moving container. Set hexa- 
gonal knob to the proper speed ( rpm ) and start motor by snapping 
toggle switch. 

A-4.2.2 After 8 to 10 revolutions press down clutch level on the back 
and shut off motor so that the dial indicator is visible. Keep clutch 
level depressed to hold the reading. Without releasing the clutch start 
motor first and then release the clutch. After the second 8 to 10 revo- 
lutions, repeat the steps above to get the check reading Make several 
check readings, allowing enough time to attain shear equilibrium 
between readings. Release clutch after shutting off motor and while 
spindle is still immersed raise instrument and remove spindle carefully 
by holding the upper shaft coupling firmly. 



Factor for spindle at different 


speeds:

Deduct 8 cps from final reading as drag correction.

Ap5. determination of AGIDITT 

A*5.0 G«ii«iml — This method determinei the acidity in styrenated 
phenol. The result is expressed in terms of percent sulphuric acid. 

A*S»I lUftg«sit0 

A-5.1.1 Mithanol 

A-5.1.2 Potassium Hydroxidi SoluHan — 0*5 N, alcoholic. 

A-5.1.3 Phinolphthaliin Indicator 

A-S*2 Procedure — Weigh 100 g of styrenated phenol to the nearest 
mg in a one litre conical flask and dissolve the contents in 500 ml of 
methanol thoroughly. Titrate the solution with 0*5 N alcoholic potas- 
sium hpdroxide using phenolphthalein as indicator. 

A-5.3 Galcvlation 

Acidity ( as H2SO4 ), percent =--= 0024 5 x ml of 0*5 N 
by mass potassium hydroxide 

A-6. DETERMINATION OF ASH CONTENT 

A-6.1 Procedure 

A»6.I«1 Heat a clean, dry, silica crucible to 550 db 25*C for 30 minutes. 
Cool in a desiccator and weigh it to the nearest mg. In the crucible 
weigh to the nearest 0*001 g about 10 g of a representative sample of the 
material under test. 

A«6«l*2 Place the crucible in the hole in the asbestos board, place the 
board on a tripod stand and heat the crucible from below with a 
Bunsen flame. Heat gently, avoiding ignition until the sample has all 
volatilised, pyrolyzed or charred. Transfer the crucible to the muffle 
furnace at 550 ± 25^C and leave for 30 minutes or longer until all the 
carbon has burnt off. Remove from the furnace, cool to room tempe- 
rature in a desiccator and weigh to the nearest O'OOl g. 

A-6.1.3 Calculation 
Ash, percent by mass ^ — jj ^ ^00 

where 

A » mass in g of the crucible; 
B = mass in g of the crucible plus ash; and 
M ^ mass In g of the sample. 

8 



IS t 7351 - 1985 

A-7. DETERMINATION OF FLASH POINT 

A-7«l Procedure — Flash point determination is carried out by the 
Pensky-M arten closed cup method as indicated in A-7-1.1* 

A-7.1.1 Thoroughly clean the cup and accessories taking care to 
remove any gasoline or naphtha used for cleaning. Fill the cup to the 
filling mark with the styrenated phenol. After locking in the lid properly, 
place the cup on the stove. Light the test flame, adjust it to 4 mm 
diameter. Rate of heating should be such that there is 60*C tempe- 
rature rise per minute. The stirrer should run at 90 to 120 rpm. Apply 
test flame at 104°C by operating the mechanism on the cover which 
controls the shutter and test flame burner so that the flame lowered into 
the vapour space of the cup in one second, left in its lowered position 
for one second and quickly raised to its high position. Continue to 
apply the flame after every 20®C rise in temperature till the flash point 
is reached. Flash point temperature is the temperature at which the 
test flame application cause a distinct flash in the interior of the cup. 

A-8. DETERMINATION OF VOLATILE MATTER 

A-8.1 Weigh 50 g of the styrenated phenol in a previously weighed 
evaporation dish. Keep the dish in vacuum at GO^'C and pressure of 
40 mm of mercury for 2 hours. Record the loss in mass. 

Volatile matter, percent by mass ^ 2 X loss in mass.
